description: The UR5e is a collaborative robot arm with six rotating joints and a medium payload. It is designed to work near people when a risk assessment supports that. In a makerspace it is used to learn robot programming and to build pick-and-place, assembly, testing and automation projects. You program it on a touchscreen teach pendant, or teach positions by moving the arm by hand in Freedrive mode. A sensor at the tool flange measures force and torque, so the arm can do tasks that need to sense contact.

specs.label: Joint speed
specs.value: max 180 °/s; tool speed approx. 1 m/s in a typical program

specs.label: Power
specs.value: 100–240 VAC, 47–440 Hz supply; 570 W max, approx. 200 W in a typical program

materials: Light parts and objects handled with a gripper or end effector, within the 5 kg payload including the tool
End effectors mounted on the ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 tool flange
useRestrictions: Only trained users may run the robot, and only after a risk assessment of the setup with the tool attached; keep the total payload under 5 kg, check that the safety settings are correct, and keep the emergency stop within reach.
